messages.subject: Counting Chirps
parts:
I'm looking for recommendations for a way that I might be able to count chirps such as the ones in this sonogram. I suspect there are probably a couple ways I could approach this task such as looking for amplitude peaks. Ideally, I would be able to differentiate multiple chirps within <.1 of a second.

Any advise that could set me on the right track would be valuable - I have only limited experience with all the functionality within seewave or other R packages for acoustic analysis.

Thanks

messages.author: 4271370c9274971b
messages.subject: Re: Counting Chirps
parts:
Logan,

Try afilter(), which allows you to set an amplitude threshold in % of the max amplitude. If you turn plot to FALSE, you can return a time series filled with zeros and values where the threshold was reached.

Sean

messages.subject: Re: Counting Chirps
parts:
I'm not sure how you'd do this, but you could probably write an if statement into the code where only one amplitude within a series is recorded - so if points at threshold are within, say 0.001 s of each other, only the first point in the series is recorded and the rest are ignored.

Let me know if you figure out a way to do it! Sorry I couldn't help more.

Sean
